incremental_scope: Native SQL prepared provenance and the new lexical effect-cycle barrier; no production edits.

blocking_findings.title: Bind can invoke planning-time routines before the Q/E-only effect barrier starts
evidence: protocol.lexical_barrier marks effects only for forwarded Q or Execute E and expressly keeps Bind available.
Pinned PostgreSQL postgres.c exec_bind_message invokes GetCachedPlan at line 2027. Pinned optimizer/util/clauses.c evaluate_function executes constant immutable function expressions during planning.
The specification trusts ordinary functions and expressly does not claim arbitrary function effect analysis; it nevertheless says the barrier protects lexical changes through a trusted routine.
blocking_findings.counterexample: Given an existing ordinary immutable routine whose execution changes standard_conforming_strings, forward an accepted Parse calling that routine, Bind it (planning can invoke the routine), then pipeline another Parse before any Execute. No Q/E is pending, so the specified barrier permits the later SQL while backend lexical mode may have changed. Async ParameterStatus monitoring cannot prevent already-forwarded bytes. Creating such a routine through the proxy is not required or authorized by this counterexample.
blocking_findings.required_change: Include all potentially effectful pre-Execute processing in barrier accounting, minimally Bind, and audit Parse analysis/type-input and Describe revalidation paths. A conservative design can mark P/B and relevant Describe as pending before forwarding, continue B/E/Sync progress, and deny subsequent new Q/P until matching validated Ready. Alternatively explicitly restrict and establish effect-freedom for every admitted pre-Execute hook; do not silently assume IMMUTABLE is an enforced side-effect guarantee.
blocking_findings.scope_limit: This is a design counterexample under the stated ordinary-function trust boundary, not a demonstrated exploit against the current owned database. No database mutation or execution probe was performed.

positive_assessments: Exact whole-source native PREPARE/EXECUTE admission, shared accepted-provenance table and cache-state separation retain the revision4 design properties.
Cycle IDs and validated completion prevent older Ready from clearing newer effects in the abstract model.
Protocol-name rejection above 63 bytes is an accepted implementation requirement from the parent review context, avoiding mixed native/protocol namespace ambiguity.

formal_assessment.conclusion: Read the entire Lean source. The six new lemmas correctly express list-based pending retention and validated removal, but cycle assignment and which messages can cause effects are trusted adapter inputs; the model cannot discharge the blocker.
formal_assessment.limits: Native body spans, normalization, backend success and Python/wire refinement remain unproved. Two clean final-hash builds and runtime gates remain required.

runtime_acceptance_required: Bind followed by a new Parse before Execute must not forward the new SQL while a planning-time lexical mutation may be pending.
Preserve all previous native name/classifier, cross-protocol, immutable portal, cache noncreation, state capacity and unchanged full ACL dump/restore tests.
Test stale Ready, delayed fragmented ParameterStatus and successful later SQL only after matching validated completion.
